title: Choose the analytics engine, a custom read model, or a relational DB by the shape of the query you need
content:
Powerhouse offers three ways to project the operation log into something queryable, and the Cookbook's Analytics Processor recipe gives the selection criterion as a table rather than a preference:

| | analytics-processor | custom-read-model | relational-db-subgraph |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Storage model | Dimensional time-series (source, metric, dimensions, unit) | In-memory map | Relational rows (Kysely schema) |
| Query style | Time-bucketed aggregates, dimension rollups via `lod` | Direct lookup | Arbitrary SQL: joins, filters, ordering |
| Best for | "Total per category per month in USD" — dashboards, budgets, spend analytics | Simple derived counts | Searchable catalogs, tag filters |

The decisive test is stated compactly: use the analytics engine when queries are shaped like *aggregate metric X, grouped by dimension Y, over period Z, rolled up to depth N*. Use a relational DB when you need relational queries. Use a custom read model for lightweight synchronous counters.

The dimensions that actually separate them are query shape and where the result lives, not data volume. A custom `IReadModel` is in-memory and synchronous, which is why it suits counters and suits nothing that must survive a restart on its own. The analytics engine is the only one of the three that understands *time intervals* natively — values carry a start and end, deltas are first class, and rollups happen at query time via `lod` — so re-bucketing "monthly" into "quarterly" needs no reprojection. A relational read model is the only one that can answer a question you did not anticipate when you designed the projection.

The analytics recipe also surfaces two modelling constraints that follow from picking it: updates and deletes must be written as **compensating entries** (−old, +new) rather than mutations, and values should be dated by *business time* (when the money was spent) rather than event or processing time, so a March correction to a January expense still lands in January.

Provenance: academy `05-Lookup/00-Cookbook.md`, Analytics Processor recipe ("When to use the analytics engine vs a SQL read model"), academy 6.2.2-dev.45.
description: Analytics engine for time-bucketed aggregates with dimension rollups, IReadModel for lightweight synchronous counters, relational DB for arbitrary SQL joins, filters and ordering.
